advances: Common frame for actual fibers at a fixed nonhollow projection.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
A common invertible affine change in the continuous coordinates, with affine translation in the base, maps the mixed lattice bijectively to itself and maps ambient halfspaces bijectively to halfspaces. All fiber volumes are multiplied by $|\det A|$, so every normalized depth is preserved.

First scale the central volume to one. Apply the maximal-inscribed-simplex normalization of accepted fact 03bc771bddd39a8a to the full-dimensional central body: it takes the body to one containing the standard simplex and contained in $[-1,1]^d$. The determinant magnitude $D$ of that map lies in $[1/d!,2^d]$ by comparing the new body volume with these two containing volumes. Translate the simplex barycenter to zero and rescale by $D^{-1/d}$, taking a reflection if needed for positive determinant. This determinant-one normalization gives
$$
\rho B_d\subset K_{z_0}\subset RB_d,qquad
\rho=1/[2(d+1)\sqrt d],\quad R=2\sqrt d\,(d!)^{1/d},
$$
since the barycenter of the standard simplex has distance at least $1/[(d+1)\sqrt d]$ to its facets and the barycenter-translated cube lies in the ball of radius $2\sqrt d$.

There are strictly positive weights $p_z$ of sum one and barycenter $z_0$: for sufficiently small $\theta>0$ write $z_0=\theta\bar z+(1-\theta)y$ with $\bar z$ the average of $P$ and $y\in\operatorname{conv}(P)$, then expand $y$. Compatibility gives $\sum_z p_zK_z\subset K_{z_0}$. Widths add under Minkowski sums, so $\operatorname{diam}K_z\le 2R/p_z$. This same inclusion shows that the central fiber has positive volume whenever any fiber has positive volume, by fixing points in the other summands.

Choose an affine basis $z_0,z_1,\ldots,z_r$ from $P$ and a point $c_i\in K_{z_i}$ at each basis site, with $c_0=0$. Choose $B$ with $B(z_i-z_0)=c_i$ for $i\ge1$ and apply $x\mapsto x-B(z-z_0)$. All basis fibers then contain zero. Choose $c_z$ from each sheared nonbasis fiber. For such $z$ write $z=\sum_{i=0}^r\lambda_i z_i$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$ and put $a^{(z)}=\delta_z-\sum_{i=0}^r\lambda_i\delta_{z_i}$ on $P$. With
$$
\varepsilon_z=\min_{v:a^{(z)}_v\ne0}p_v/(2|a^{(z)}_v|)>0,
$$
the weights $p\pm\varepsilon_z a^{(z)}$ remain positive with sum one and barycenter $z_0$. Their chosen-point averages both belong to $K_{z_0}$ and differ by $2\varepsilon_z c_z$. Hence $\|c_z\|\le R/\varepsilon_z$. The basis fibers lie in their diameter balls, and all other fibers lie in balls of radius $R/\varepsilon_z+2R/p_z$. All constants can be fixed from $P,d$ by fixing the weights and bases once for each possible $z_0$ in the finite set.

source_sections.locator: a14cc5f809b2b766:01 §§1–3, volume-preserving normalization and uniform bounds

statement: Let $d\ge1$, $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty, and $z_0\in P\cap\operatorname{relint}\operatorname{conv}(P)$. Let $(K_z)_{z\in P}$ be nonempty compact convex sets that are the actual fibers of the convex hull of their lifts. If $|K_{z_0}|>0$, maps of the form $(z,x)\mapsto(z,Ax+Bz+b)$ with $A\in\operatorname{GL}(d,\mathbb R)$ can normalize $|K_{z_0}|$ to one and put all fibers in a common centered ball depending only on $P,d$. If the central volume is already one, the maps can have determinant one. No bounds on other fiber volumes are required.
title: A bounded affine normalization over a fixed projection with an interior lattice site
